what: Bit decomposition at its own width against Bulletproofs at the width it rounds up to, both in Rust on one machine.
why: DEPLOYMENT.md reported 6.3x on verification and 10.5x on package, but that pair was Python bit decomposition against Rust Bulletproofs, so the scheme was confounded with the language. Both are in Rust now.
finding: The language was not the confound. At the calibration width of 40 bits Bulletproofs at 64 verifies 6.2x faster and is 11.4x smaller, and proving is a dead heat. Bit decomposition wins at no width.
decision: Single-prover range proofs use Bulletproofs. The calibration pair moves from a 40-bit bit decomposition to a 64-bit Bulletproof, and every timing is re-taken against it.
where_bit_decomposition_survives: The threshold form only. A range proof commits to each bit, extracting bits needs the value, and a node holding a share cannot do that, so Bulletproofs cannot be assembled from shares at all.
prediction_before_measuring: Bulletproofs wins on size and verify; bit decomposition might win on prove. The last part was wrong: 9.575 against 9.565 ms is a tie.
